headline: High: Airbyte’s broad egress paired with Taipy’s default-unknown orchestration creates a plausible data-leak and cascading-error path; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but not absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not proven. However, Airbyte can move data through APIs and Taipy is a data-engineering/scheduler tool, so if an operator bridges them via files or messages, Taipy could ingest attacker-controlled content from Airbyte outputs. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not observed.
conditions: IF the operator connects Airbyte outputs to Taipy inputs via files, queues, or copied text
IF Taipy treats imported content as instructions or parameters without validation
mitigations: Use a strict schema for any Airbyte-to-Taipy handoff
Disable automatic execution of text-derived commands
Add a manual review step before Taipy consumes Airbyte outputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress, while Taipy has no documented egress and no data classes listed. The pair can still leak if Airbyte exports sensitive business data into a shared workspace or downstream channel that Taipy reads and renders. This is plausible in default integration patterns, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Airbyte is configured to extract sensitive business data into a location Taipy can read
IF Taipy displays or forwards that content without redaction
mitigations: Restrict Airbyte sources to non-sensitive datasets
Keep Airbyte and Taipy on separate workspaces
Redact fields before Taipy ingests them
Audit outbound destinations from Airbyte
requires-engineering: enforce per-dataset access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents are data-engineering tools, but only Airbyte shows explicit API/network capability and Taipy has no write surfaces or mutable-resource scopes documented. Without evidence of overlapping write access to the same resource, conflict is limited to unusual orchestration setups. Uncertainty is low enough to stay at low rather than medium.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same external dataset or API
IF an orchestrator does not serialize their updates
mitigations: Assign separate target resources to each agent
Run one writer at a time
Add locking around shared datasets
Review any shared OAuth or API credentials
requires-engineering: implement optimistic concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce transformed business data, and Taipy is positioned for automation and scheduling, so Taipy may treat Airbyte outputs as authoritative inputs. There is no documented verification boundary between them, making a mistaken upstream extraction or transformation propagate into downstream actions or reports. The pathway is plausible by default integration, though not directly observed.
conditions: IF Taipy consumes Airbyte-produced datasets or metrics without validation
IF downstream workflows act on those datasets automatically
mitigations: Insert a validation step between Airbyte and Taipy
Require human approval for downstream actions
Compare sampled records against source systems
Log and alert on schema drift
requires-engineering: add automated reconciliation checks

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte explicitly touches business data and has broad egress, while Taipy’s residency, retention, and certification posture is undocumented. If regulated business data flows from Airbyte into Taipy, mismatched logging or retention could create a compliance gap. Because only one agent’s data handling is described, the risk is inferred and stays medium.
conditions: IF regulated business data is routed from Airbyte into Taipy
IF Taipy stores, logs, or exports that data under different retention rules
mitigations: Classify the data before routing it
Avoid sending regulated data to Taipy
Check retention settings on both systems
Document the data flow for audit purposes
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies
